note: The substantive work this re-review exists to check holds up under direct verification against primary sources. All four previously-unanchored folds (positional identity, silent resource downgrade, reuse-detector semantics, multilingual leakage) now cite named POSED releases, and I opened posed-plugin's CHANGELOG.md at 2ca8f7b and confirmed every one of the load-bearing quotes verbatim -- these are genuine anchors, not relabeled guesses. The f3 attribution correction (AI reviewer, not human gate, cited the forged report) is accurate and independently confirmed against the 1.35/1.38 entries. The f3<->f8 dependency cycle is gone (no depends_on field references another row id anywhere in the ledger), ids are never recycled, and a full programmatic check of all 31 rows found no missing required fields, no dangling superseded_by references, and row_accounting's stated totals (31/28/3) match the actual data exactly. The Stage-8-versus-release-history relabeling is consistent everywhere I looked in both documents; no stray 'Stage 8 pilot harvest' framing survives. All twelve Codex recommendations resolve to a traceable row or absorption inside the ledger itself. What I found instead is smaller-scale residue from the scripted split: two stale cross-references to superseded rows (the CR's section 5 still cites f17 for three Codex recommendations that section 4 of the same document correctly reassigns to f28/f29/f30, and ledger row f11 still cites f8 for a fold that now lives in f21), a literal ellipsis surviving in two of the newest rows' anchors despite an explicit claim that ellipsis paths were resolved, a consistency gap where five split-out rows (f19-f23) lost the specific lesson-number citation their siblings carry, and a latent dependency between f5 and f31 that the ledger's 'independent_of_other_rows' flag does not actually capture. None of these change any row's substance or evidence; all are two-line, mechanical fixes. Given zero blocking-severity findings and full independent confirmation of everything the first review flagged as unresolved, the gate should open, with the two major findings patched promptly so the CR and the ledger stop pointing to a row marked 'do not gate on it.'
